summary:
Shackleton Crater and the Connecting Ridge (89.9° S). Using real NASA LRO/LOLA topography (20 m/px) and 720-hour NASA/JPL Horizons ephemeris data, it models curvature-aware 360° horizon masks, partial solar disc illumination, solar array power output, Direct-to-Earth geometric line-of-sight, and DSN complex visibility.

It directly addresses the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge—alongside Earth Analogs and Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer tracks—by uniting real-time GLSL slope-hazard and thermal/PSR proxy overlays, multi-site A/B/C comparison, a multi-criteria Site Finder, A* rover traverse planning, 3-sigma landing ellipses, and a 2 m first-person Explorer mode in a browser-based WebGL/Web Worker architecture.

Selecting an Artemis-era south-pole landing site requires balancing near-continuous solar power and Earth communications against steep crater slopes and extreme cold traps. RegolithForge makes these complex orbital, terrain, and engineering trade-offs transparent, verifiable, and accessible to both mission planners and learners.
details:
RegolithForge is an offline-first, interactive 3D lunar south-pole landing-site navigator and mission trainer centered on Shackleton Crater and the Connecting Ridge (89.9° S).

  1. Offline NASA Data Pipeline (REAL Provenance): A Python pipeline pre-processes a 1024×1024 Float32 slice (20.48 km × 20.48 km at 20 m/px) of NASA LRO/LOLA south-polar topography (LDEM_875S_20M) in Polar Stereographic projection and pairs it with a 720-hour NASA/JPL Horizons airless lunar-surface ephemeris (observer_body = 301, 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-30, 1-hour steps) for Sun/Earth azimuth, elevation, and range.
  2. Curvature-Aware Horizon & Solar Power Engine (DERIVED): A 360° terrain horizon raycaster accounts for lunar curvature drop (h_eff(d) = h(d) - d²/(2R), R = 1,737,400 m), solar disc partial illumination (~0.533° angular diameter), and (1 AU / r)² irradiance scaling. Users can test vertical azimuth-tracking, fixed horizontal, and two-axis tracking solar arrays at mast heights from 0 m to 30 m.
  3. Direct-to-Earth (DTE) Communications: Computes geometric line-of-sight (Geometric LOS), one-way light time (~1.28 s), free-space path loss (FSPL), and visibility to NASA Deep Space Network (DSN) complexes in Goldstone, Madrid, and Canberra.
    • GLSL Shader Overlays: Real-time slope hazard grading (adjustable threshold, default 15°) and derived Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR) / thermal proxies.
    • Planning Tools: Multi-site A/B/C comparison (including benchmark Artemis-region sites: Connecting Ridge Primary, Shackleton Crater Rim, and de Gerlache Ridge Rim), multi-criteria Site Finder, A* rover traverse planner with an animated 3D rover, 3-sigma landing uncertainty ellipse, and an Earth analog comparison modal.
    • Explorer Mode (2 m): A first-person surface view with guided learner challenges for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer track.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Accessible Mission Trade-Off Analysis: Makes complex orbital, terrain, power, and communications trade-offs immediately visual and interactive in any modern browser—no specialized desktop GIS or astrodynamics software required.
  • Offline-First & Fast: Pre-cached binary terrain and ephemeris assets combined with Web Workers (for horizon, scoring, and A* pathfinding) allow smooth, responsive exploration even without an active internet connection.
  • Dual-Purpose Impact: Supports both technical mission-planning workflows (evaluating landing safety, traverse cost, and illumination windows) and STEM education (teaching students why Artemis-era missions target the lunar south pole and how lunar conditions compare to Earth analogs).

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & 3D Rendering: React 18, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei), custom GLSL fragment shaders
  • State, UI & Charts: Zustand, Tailwind CSS v4, Recharts, Lucide React
  • Performance & Concurrency: Web Workers, Vite
  • Offline Data Pipeline: Python (numpy, rasterio, pyproj, requests)
  • Testing & Deployment: Vitest (unit tests verifying astrodynamics math and 3D-vs-HUD consistency), Python pipeline tests, Netlify

What Makes RegolithForge Creative

  • Strict Provenance & Honesty: Instead of hiding approximations, RegolithForge explicitly labels REAL NASA/JPL inputs versus DERIVED calculations and surfaces known engineering limits right in the UI (e.g., DEM-resolution-limited (20 m/px) warnings and Geometric LOS vs. full RF link budget distinctions).
  • One Engine, Two Perspectives: Seamlessly switches (E key) between an orbital/tactical Mission Planner and a 2 m Explorer view where users experience the low-angle polar sun and horizon shadows at human/rover scale.
  • Earth Analog Bridge: Connects lunar south-pole terrain and illumination challenges directly to terrestrial analog environments inside the same workflow.

Factors Our Team Considered

  • Scientific & Physical Accuracy: Lunar curvature drop over long sightlines, partial solar disc occlusion (0.533°), and 1-hour ephemeris stepping across a full 29.53-day synodic month.
  • Accessibility & Usability: Okabe-Ito color-blind-safe palette toggle, keyboard navigation (Space, ←/→, E, P), and prefers-reduced-motion support.
  • Performance & Responsiveness: Offloading heavy terrain raycasting, site scoring, and A* pathfinding to Web Workers so the 3D WebGL scene remains fluid.
  • Data Attribution & Compliance: Full attribution to NASA LRO/LOLA (LDEM_875S_20M) and NASA/JPL Horizons (observer_body = 301), clear non-affiliation disclaimer, and transparent disclosure of AI-assisted development with automated verification.
